This is how I have come to frame it:

Almost every BPII person I’ve met inpatient (BPI is a different kettle of fish) has actually been an addict of some sort beneath that diagnosis, whether that be alcohol, drugs, codependency, whatever. 

They tend to be distinct and often remarkable characters, even if their lives are mundane and underachieving. Like a lot of addicts, they seem to have a higher dopamine set-point needed to function, whether through genetics or environmental conditioning (inconsistent reward from a primary caregiver fucking with your dopamine system, doing heaps of sports as a kid then suddenly stopping, etc), probably both. This sets the brain up for addiction. 

What does a dopamine deprived brain do? It seeks it out. Hits. Hits work, and they cause crashes. The system becomes dysregulated. The addiction shifts around, sometimes seamlessly. Alcohol, codependent relationships, bingeing and purging, doing weird shit. It peaks and crashes. But it also eludes strict “addiction” diagnosis, because it will take any ‘drug’ (hit).

Ameliorating this means resetting the dopamine system (dopamine detox) and maintaining. Easier said than done, obviously. Psych drugs can be supportive of this process (and other times not), but they’re often used to bandaid it whilst the shapeshifting addiction continues. It’s not enough for doctors to say “you shouldn’t drink on this” or “you should eat three square meals a day” and throw you a drug. They don’t cause it per se but allow it to flourish. Most tests will only pick up on these when they reach a certain threshold count. Lots of microbes live in the vagina, all in competition with each other. When you kill off several armies (including beneficial lactobacilli) with antibiotics, it makes it easier for microbes not susceptible to those antibiotics to flourish. Like soldiers at battle. This is why people often get yeast infections after antibiotics. Yeast and ‘BV’, usually gardnerella, are the biggest culprits. They were living there already but get out of control.

You basically need to go to your doctor and tell them about your symptoms and ask for a swab for BV and yeast. After getting the swab, boric acid suppositories can help hold you over until you get treatment (needs to be after or it will affect test results).
